reason: The text (Ezekiel 37:11-14, the Valley of Dry Bones vision) explicitly states that the dry bones represent 'the whole house of Israel' (כָּל־ בֵּית יִשְׂרָאֵל), and God addresses them collectively as 'my people' (עַמִּי) without distinction of elite or regular classes. The restoration promised is universal—all Israel are to be revived and restored together. The passage emphasizes equality before God and inclusive restoration, directly contradicting the idea that any elite class is inherently superior.
